Specify the list of input subjects from the fsgd file.

statement: The --target option selects the common-space subject; --hemi selects lh or rh for source and target surfaces.
quote:
--target subject
Subject to use as the common-space. All the input data will be resampled to the surface of this subject.
--hemi hemi
Use hemi for source and target surfaces. hemi can be lh or rh.

statement: When subjects are listed using --s, each has its own --s; this option is for use with --meas.
quote:
--s subjN
Specify an input subject on the command-line. All subjects must be specified in this way on the command-line (ie, each with its own --s). For use with --meas.

statement: The --is option is an alternative to --meas and still requires a supplied subject list.
quote:
--is surfmeasfile
Specify full path to input surface measure file. This is an alternative to using --meas. This still requires that a subject list be supplied.

statement: For --paired-diff there must be an even number of inputs.
quote:
--paired-diff
After concatenating all the inputs together, create a new output file by computing paired differences, ie, Input1-Input2, Input3-Input4, etc. There must be an even number of inputs.

statement: When using full paths with --fsgd, subjects must be in the same order as the input surface files.
quote:
Same as #1 but using full paths. Note there is no --meas, but
--fsgd still needed to provide list of subjects, which must be in the same order as the --isp.

statement: --cache-out-only requires supplying a tmpdir.
quote: If you want to cache without actually creating an output, then --cache-out-only. You must supply a tmpdir.

statement: ANALYZE and NIFTI formats cannot represent a dimension with more than 32k elements.
quote: This will not work for ANALYZE and NIFTI formats because they cannot represent a dimension with more than 32k elements.

quote: None of the paired diff options will affect caching.
